headline: A suspected Chinese espionage group held a VMware vCenter zero-day for more than two months before Broadcom shipped a fix, while another China-linked crew turned the Cairn AI framework loose on two universities and it surfaced a zero-day of its own.

emerging_trends.text: Offensive AI frameworks have crossed from automating known attack steps into finding new bugs, with Cairn surfacing an apparent zero-day in a medical imaging application and Artex serving as the way into the European Commission.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Cairn Finds a Zero-Day in a Medical Imaging App

emerging_trends.text: Suppliers now carry the breach for everyone downstream, as the N0n extortion group's leak pushed JPMorgan, Visa, and Mastercard to point at third-party providers, N-able traced a worldwide mail outage to an attacker on one of its servers, and 40-plus Irish credit unions filed notifications over Wellington IT.
emerging_trends.topic_title: N0n Leak Pulls In JPMorgan, Visa, and Mastercard

emerging_trends.text: Network edge gear absorbs the week's pressure from both directions: F5 rushed emergency BIG-IP fixes, attackers took Cisco Expressway clusters days after a proof of concept went public, and SonicWall told Gen 6 owners to junk the hardware because automated scanning finds unsupported devices faster than owners can defend them.
emerging_trends.topic_title: F5, Ruby, and SonicWall Force an Edge Patch Cycle

topics.title: Armory Castle Owns the vCenter Zero-Day
topics.latest_developments: Google Threat Intelligence Group attributed the zero-day exploitation of CVE-2026-123890 to Armory Castle, the suspected China-nexus espionage group formerly tracked as UNC5221, which has used the authentication bypass since at least early September 2026—more than two months before Broadcom released a fix—to take administrative sessions on vCenter Server and steal data.
topics.summary: CVE-2026-123890, rated 9.8, lets a remote, unauthenticated attacker bypass authentication in the VMware Directory Service and seize vCenter, the console that manages an organization's ESX hosts and virtual machines. Broadcom has shipped fixed builds for every supported branch and lists no workaround, so patch now and hunt for September activity.

sources.title: China-Linked Hackers Exploit Critical VMware vCenter Zero-Day to Gain Admin Access and Steal Data
VMware patches vCenter zero-day exploited in attacks since September
VMware vCenter zero-day exploited for months before patch (CVE-2026-123890)
Newly Patched VMware vCenter Flaw Exploited as Zero-Day by Chinese APT

topics.title: SBC Medical Group Count Passes 2 Million
topics.latest_developments: SBC Medical Group raised its count past 2 million people after threat actors reached databases holding customer information tied to its clinics in Japan, N-able attributed the worldwide outage of its Mail Assure and SpamExperts Hosted Cloud to attackers who breached one of its servers and may have taken customer credentials, Transport for London said it spotted suspicious activity on its photocard site on November 16, 2026 and took the system offline, and Ireland's Data Protection Commission said it has received more than 40 breach notifications from credit unions that used the Belfast company Wellington IT as a data processor, a compromise that ran six weeks before anyone noticed.
topics.summary: SBC Medical Group told the United States Securities and Exchange Commission that two incidents exposed customer and employee data; the Transport for London breach touches roughly 265,000 Oyster photocard holders, among them children with Zip cards and Londoners holding the 60+ London Oyster photocard. N-able customers should rotate credentials used with the hosted mail services.

sources.title: SBC Medical Group Data Breach Impacts Over 2 Million
N-able Blames Service Disruption on Cyberattack
265,000 Oyster photocard customers’ data exposed in Transport for London breach
Dozens of credit unions hit by supplier breach that went unnoticed for six weeks

topics.title: F5, Ruby, and SonicWall Force an Edge Patch Cycle
topics.latest_developments: F5 issued emergency patches for five critical BIG-IP flaws that attackers can drive into denial of service or remote code execution, Ruby fixed CVE-2026-132825, a heap-based buffer overflow that researchers call Ruby2Shell and that can carry an attacker to code execution, and SonicWall told every Gen 6 firewall owner to retire the hardware immediately because automated, AI-assisted scanning finds unsupported edge devices faster than ever.
topics.summary: BIG-IP sits in front of corporate applications, Ruby runs the web stack behind many of them, and SonicOS 6.x now receives no firmware or security updates at any severity. Patch BIG-IP and Ruby, and pull Gen 6 and Gen 6.5 appliances off the internet edge.

sources.title: F5 releases emergency patches for critical BIG-IP RCE flaws
Ruby Patches Ruby2Shell Vulnerability That Could Lead to RCE
SonicWall Warns Gen 6 Firewalls Won't Get Security Patches, Even for Critical Flaws

topics.title: Cairn Finds a Zero-Day in a Medical Imaging App
topics.latest_developments: Amazon's threat intelligence researchers reported that a China-linked threat actor drove Cairn, the open-source AI penetration-testing framework, through persistent attacks on two universities, and that in one case the tool turned up a previously unknown vulnerability in a medical imaging application and took over the server.
topics.summary: Cairn chains reconnaissance, exploitation, and follow-on actions with little human direction, and it joins Artex, CyberStrikeAI, and PentAGI as frameworks state-backed crews already run operationally. Defenders should expect bug discovery at machine speed against niche applications that no vendor patch cycle covers quickly, and watch internet-facing clinical and research software closely.

sources.title: Hackers use autonomous AI tool Cairn to find zero-day, take over server
Amazon says Chinese hackers used Cairn AI tool to discover apparent zero-day during attack on university

topics.title: European Commission Confirms an AI-Assisted Intrusion
topics.latest_developments: Commission spokesperson Thomas Regnier confirmed the attack at Thursday's midday press briefing in Brussels, saying the intruders misused a publicly available AI tool, that the Commission pulled several applications offline to contain the incident, and that it has found no evidence anyone took data.
topics.summary: CERT-EU, the computer emergency response team for the European Union institutions, identified the attackers' tool as Artex, the open-source AI hacking platform the FBI warned about in the hands of criminals and state-sponsored groups. Reporters pressed Regnier on which systems went down and whether staff data moved, and he confined himself to the containment steps.

sources.title: European Commission Confirms AI-Assisted Cyberattack Disrupted Services
European Commission confirms AI-generated cyberattack disrupted its systems

topics.title: N0n Leak Pulls In JPMorgan, Visa, and Mastercard
topics.latest_developments: J.P. Morgan Chase warned customers that a cyberattack at a third-party service provider exposed their personal information and marketing data, hardening what began as a claim by the N0n extortion group, which published data it says belongs to customers of JPMorgan, Visa, and Mastercard; all three companies attribute the exposure to outside providers.
topics.summary: N0n runs a leak-site extortion operation and has now named three of the largest names in American finance and card payments. Banks and card networks should map which vendors hold cardholder and account records and demand incident timelines from them.

sources.title: JPMorgan, Visa, Mastercard Cite Third-Party Incidents Amid Data Leak
Vendor data breach exposes Chase, Visa, Mastercard customer info

topics.title: ROMULUS ClickFix Delivers a New Remote Access Trojan
topics.latest_developments: Blackpoint researchers reported that the ROMULUS ClickFix platform now drops a previously undocumented remote access trojan that spies on users and controls their PCs, and that ROMULUS runs as a delivery service pushing CNCMachineRMS and Legion Loader through separate chains; the Dutch firm ThreatFabric separately disclosed Bazuka, an Android malware framework it found in late October 2026 while investigating an NFC-relay banking trojan, which wires a large language model into victim management and hides credential theft behind fake screen overlays.
topics.summary: ClickFix lures a user into pasting a command that supposedly fixes a broken page, and ROMULUS pairs that trick with signed binary sideloading to get its payloads past endpoint controls. The new trojan resembles CNCMachineRMS; defenders should block clipboard-to-run-dialog behavior and audit which signed binaries load unexpected libraries.

sources.title: ROMULUS ClickFix Attacks Deliver RAT That Can Spy on Users and Control PCs
Bazuka Android Malware Uses Fake Screen Overlays to Hide Credential Theft and Device Control

topics.title: Cisco Expressway Falls to a Public Proof of Concept
topics.latest_developments: Attackers exploited CVE-2026-76466, the Cisco Expressway flaw rated 9.8, within days of a public proof of concept, breaching four clustered devices at a Russian organization, reaching the internal network, and staging tooling for lateral movement.
topics.summary: Expressway carries video calls and collaboration traffic at the network edge, and the bug hands an unauthenticated attacker with network access a way past authentication. Patch every node, then inspect clustered peers for attacker tooling, because compromising one member of a cluster exposes the rest.

sources.title: Hackers Exploit Critical Cisco Expressway Flaw, Breach Four Devices and Reach Internal Network

topics.title: Cairncross Leaves the White House Cyber Post
topics.latest_developments: Sean Cairncross is leaving the White House as national cyber director, and Kirsten Davies, the Pentagon's chief information officer, takes the job in an acting capacity as the administration resets its cyber leadership.
topics.summary: The Office of the National Cyber Director writes federal cyber strategy, coordinates agencies, and speaks for the White House to industry on incidents and regulation. The handoff lands while President Trump's pick to run the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, LoSapio, still awaits Senate confirmation, leaving both top civilian cyber roles unsettled.

sources.title: Cyber Director Cairncross out as White House resets cyber leadership

topics.title: Linux KVM Hands Guests the Host's Memory
topics.latest_developments: Researchers used CVE-2026-99312, a flaw in KVM, the hypervisor built into the Linux kernel, to read roughly 127 gigabytes of a DigitalOcean server's memory from inside a virtual machine of their own, which on a shared host can include other customers' virtual machines.
topics.summary: The flaw reaches only hosts running AMD processors with nested virtualization turned on, and fixed kernels have shipped. Cloud operators and anyone running their own KVM hypervisors should roll out the patched kernels and turn off nested virtualization where no workload needs it.

sources.title: Linux KVM Flaw CVE-2026-99312 Lets Guest VMs Access Host Memory on AMD Hosts

business_politics.title: The AI Selloff Deepens and Metals Break Down
business_politics.latest_developments: The rout carried the S&P 500 and the Dow industrials into correction territory Friday, November 20, Anthropic shares fell as much as 13% a day after the stock's debut, gold and silver hit their lowest prices in more than a year, and crude headed for a third straight weekly loss as the dollar edged lower.
business_politics.summary: Anthropic's record $81 billion initial public offering, priced at $83 a share and up 17% on its first Nasdaq session Thursday, November 19, failed to steady the artificial-intelligence trade: the Nikkei dropped 2.9% behind chip and metals shares, European AI names fell sharply, and the S&P 500 now runs its longest losing streak since 2020. Traders betting on tighter Federal Reserve policy drove gold and silver down, overwhelming the usual safe-haven bid, which leaves banks and asset managers marking losses across both the AI equity complex and the metals hedge against it.

business_politics.title: Washington Clears Advanced AI Chips for China
business_politics.latest_developments: Senator Tom Cotton of Arkansas told the Wall Street Journal Friday, November 20, that Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick repeatedly ignored his warnings that Nvidia chips were reaching China through smugglers, and President Trump said the same day that American companies building artificial-intelligence data centers abroad will pay "a tremendous tax."
business_politics.summary: The Financial Times reported Friday, November 20, that the United States approved sales of advanced artificial-intelligence chips to Chinese companies, which cuts against the Commerce Department rule issued Monday, November 16, that tightened shipments of Nvidia and other American chips to China and pushed Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company and Samsung Electronics to suspend some Chinese orders. Export policy now swings in both directions inside one week, which scrambles revenue forecasts for the chipmakers and the trade financing built around them.

business_politics.title: The Senate Passes a Permitting Overhaul
business_politics.latest_developments: The Senate passed bipartisan permitting legislation Thursday, November 19, and sent it to the House, the first major act of Congress since the midterm elections.
business_politics.summary: The bill speeds federal permitting reviews for power plants, transmission lines, mining, and other energy infrastructure and makes data centers pay for the energy costs they add, and it split Democrats who argue it weakens environmental protection laws. Surging data center demand now drives load growth across the American grid, and the measure aims at both new supply and lower electricity prices for consumers.

sources.title: Senate Passes Measure Designed to Speed Up Energy Projects, Lower Consumer Costs
The Senate passed a bipartisan bill designed to speed up energy, mining and other infrastructure projects, overcoming concerns among many Democrats that it would weaken environmental protection laws

business_politics.title: Russia Hits Kyiv's Bridges
business_politics.latest_developments: Russian missiles and drones hammered targets across Ukraine overnight into Friday, November 20, damaging bridges in Kyiv after Vladimir Putin vowed retaliation for this week's Ukrainian strike on the Crimean bridge, and the Financial Times reported the same day that United States officials want an agreement between Putin and President Volodymyr Zelenskyy signed before Democrats take over Congress in January.
business_politics.summary: The barrage followed the first meeting ever to put President Trump, Xi Jinping, and Vladimir Putin in one room, which closed Thursday, November 19, in Shenzhen with a joint denunciation of nuclear war and no breakthrough on Ukraine. Trump's envoys, among them Jared Kushner, have discussed giving Ukraine NATO membership in exchange for surrendering territory in the Donbas, a reversal of longstanding United States policy, and the renewed strikes on the Ukrainian capital show Putin pressing his terms.

business.title: Beam Takes Over UPMC's Hospital Division
business.latest_developments: Alison Beam becomes acting president of UPMC's Health Services division, the system's hospital arm, TribLive reported Friday, November 20, as UPMC opens a search for a permanent president.
business.summary: Beam served as acting Pennsylvania health secretary during part of the covid-19 pandemic and now runs the division that operates the hospitals of UPMC, the Pittsburgh nonprofit that anchors health care employment across Western Pennsylvania. The interim appointment puts the system's largest business under temporary leadership while the search runs.

sources.title: UPMC taps acting president of hospital division as search for permanent replacement begins

business.title: ShadoBeni Closes on the North Side
business.latest_developments: ShadoBeni, the North Side restaurant that served vegan Trinidadian food, has closed for good and blamed rising costs, WPXI reported Friday, November 20.
business.summary: The restaurant built a following on Pittsburgh's North Side around Trinidadian cooking without meat or dairy. Its owners cited the cost of operating as the reason for shutting the doors permanently.

sources.title: North Side vegan restaurant ShadoBeni closes for good, cites rising costs

business.title: Rice and Sheehan Take the CBS Buyout
business.latest_developments: TribLive's TV Talk reported Friday, November 20, that KDKA-TV anchor Ken Rice and investigative reporter Andy Sheehan accepted the voluntary buyout CBS offered employees this week and will leave the station.
business.summary: Rice anchors KDKA-TV's 5, 6, and 11 p.m. newscasts and Sheehan has worked the investigative beat for decades, and both exit under the buyout that followed Skydance's takeover of CBS. Their departures strip two of the most recognized faces from Pittsburgh's oldest television newsroom.

sources.title: TV Talk: Ken Rice and Andy Sheehan take Skydance buyout, will exit KDKA-TV

business.title: Big Beaver Weighs a Data Center on a Racetrack Site
business.latest_developments: Residents pressed their objections at a Big Beaver Borough meeting Thursday, November 19, raising concerns that ranged to the hearing of children who live nearby.
business.summary: Developers want to build a data center on a former racetrack property in Big Beaver Borough, Beaver County, and the borough meeting turned into a hearing on noise and quality of life. The fight mirrors data center siting disputes elsewhere in Western Pennsylvania, including the ordinance Buffalo Township drafted so neighbors would not hear, smell, or see such a building.

sources.title: Concerns about data center plan include children's hearing at latest meeting in Big Beaver Borough

business.title: A 255-Unit Townhome Plan Stalls in Penn Hills
business.latest_developments: The Penn Hills planning commission put off discussion of the 255-unit townhouse development Thursday, November 19, citing deficiencies in the application, and sent a packed room of residents home within minutes.
business.summary: Residents filled the Penn Hills municipal building expecting to argue over the project, which would add 255 townhouses to the Allegheny County municipality. The incomplete application pushes the review to a later meeting and delays the largest residential proposal Penn Hills has seen in years.

sources.title: 255-unit townhome project stalls in Penn Hills planning commission because of 'deficiencies' with application

around_town.title: A Sinkhole Cuts Water in Pleasant Hills
around_town.latest_developments: A broken underground valve opened a sinkhole in a busy Pleasant Hills intersection Friday morning, November 20, closing part of the roadway and shutting off running water to nearby homes.
around_town.summary: The failure in Pleasant Hills, the Allegheny County borough south of Pittsburgh, blocked traffic through the intersection and left residents without water while crews worked the repair. It follows water main breaks this month in Baldwin and Jefferson Hills.

sources.title: Sinkhole opens up in busy Pleasant Hills intersection, cutting water to residents

around_town.title: Half the Graves Lack Wreaths at the Alleghenies Cemetery
around_town.latest_developments: Wreaths Across America has raised money for only half the graves at the National Cemetery of the Alleghenies and asked the public Friday, November 20, to sponsor the remaining 9,500.
around_town.summary: The organization places a wreath on every veteran's grave at the national cemetery each December and now runs 9,500 short of that goal. Sponsorships from the public decide whether those graves get a wreath this season.

sources.title: Help needed to secure wreaths for every veteran's grave at National Cemetery of the Alleghenies

around_town.title: Old Christmas Lights Pay for Project Bundle-Up
around_town.latest_developments: WTAE published the list of Michael Brothers drop-off locations Friday, November 20, where Pittsburgh-area residents can leave burned-out and tangled Christmas lights to raise money for Project Bundle-Up.
around_town.summary: Michael Brothers collects the used light strands at its locations around the Pittsburgh region, and the proceeds go to Project Bundle-Up, which buys winter coats for children and older adults across Western Pennsylvania. The drive runs as households untangle their decorations for the season.

sources.title: Michael Brothers collecting used Christmas lights for Project Bundle-Up

around_town.title: The Turnpike Staffs Every Plaza With Interpreters
around_town.latest_developments: The Pennsylvania Turnpike Commission announced Friday, November 20, that it now provides free visual and American Sign Language interpreting services for travelers at all 17 of its service plazas, days before the Thanksgiving rush.
around_town.summary: The service covers every plaza on the 565-mile toll road, including the Oakmont, New Stanton, and Zelienople stops that Western Pennsylvania drivers use, and reaches blind and deaf travelers who need help reading signage or speaking with plaza staff. The commission put the program in place as holiday traffic builds across the commonwealth.

sources.title: Pennsylvania Turnpike adds free services for blind, deaf travelers at all plazas

around_town.title: The 2027 Budgets Split on Taxes
around_town.latest_developments: WPXI reported Friday, November 20, that Oakmont officials tie their proposed 17% real estate tax increase to the cost of severe storms, while Westmoreland County commissioners unveiled a deficit budget Thursday, November 19, with no tax increase, and Bradford Woods put forward a $2.6 million budget that holds taxes flat.
around_town.summary: Oakmont property owners in Allegheny County face the steepest increase of the three, Westmoreland County's commissioners pledged no tax hike while running a deficit, and Bradford Woods leans on a new local services tax for added revenue. The three documents show municipalities around Pittsburgh choosing among tax increases, new levies, and deficits as 2027 budget season closes.

around_town.title: Sto-Rox Teachers Carry the Fight to the Board
around_town.latest_developments: Teachers rallied at the Sto-Rox school board meeting Thursday night, November 19, urging the board to finalize a contract, a day after the union voted to authorize a strike.
around_town.summary: The Sto-Rox Education Association has worked 142 days under an expired contract in the district that serves McKees Rocks and Stowe Township, and its members authorized a walkout Wednesday, November 18, while holding off on setting a date. The rally puts direct pressure on the board to settle before a strike interrupts classes.

sources.title: Sto-Rox teachers rally at board meeting after authorizing potential strike

around_town.title: A Warm Weekend, Then a Turn Cooler
around_town.latest_developments: Pittsburgh climbs into the low to mid 60s Friday afternoon, November 20, under a fourth straight day of sunshine, and KDKA puts cooler air into next week.
around_town.summary: WPXI and WTAE hold the sunshine and unusual warmth across Western Pennsylvania through the start of the weekend, which gives homeowners a dry window for outdoor holiday lights ahead of Light Up Night. The cooldown arrives as Thanksgiving week begins.

events.summary: The 65th annual Highmark Light Up Night opens Pittsburgh's holiday season Saturday, November 21, across downtown, with the holiday market that opened Friday, November 20, in Market Square, and Pittsburgh Regional Transit detouring 50 bus routes around the festivities.

events.title: Goose Plays Two Nights at the Wylie
events.latest_developments: TribLive reviewed the first of Goose's two nights at Citizens Live at the Wylie in a piece published Friday morning, November 20, with the second show still to come.
events.summary: The jam band Goose stretched 13 songs across three and a half hours at Citizens Live at the Wylie, Pittsburgh's newest large music room, and drew a crowd willing to stand through all of it. The band returns for the second night of the stand.

around_teams.title: Tomlin Settles the Jacoby Jones Story
around_teams.latest_developments: Not Just Football with Cam Heyward posted the full Mike Tomlin segment Friday morning, November 20, a week after the show teased it with a clip.
around_teams.summary: Tomlin, the former Steelers head coach, tells Cameron Heyward and co-host Hayden what happened on the Jacoby Jones kickoff return that drew him a $100,000 fine for stepping toward the field, and the show cut a companion short Thursday, November 19, calling the sequence one of the biggest what-ifs in Steelers history.

around_teams.latest_developments: The Steelers posted video late Thursday, November 19, of head coach Mike McCarthy's news conference before that afternoon's practice.
around_teams.summary: McCarthy met reporters for the second time during Week 11 preparation as the 6-3 Steelers get ready to visit the Philadelphia Eagles Sunday, November 22, at 1 p.m. Eastern on CBS, a building where Pittsburgh has not won since the Lyndon Johnson administration.

team_usa.title: Pochettino's USMNT Send-Off
team_usa.latest_developments: ESPN published its account of Mauricio Pochettino's farewell to the United States men's national team Friday, November 20, and Pochettino, presented at Old Trafford the same day, said he wants a say in Manchester United's transfer decisions.
team_usa.summary: Pochettino left the United States job on his own terms after Christian Pulisic's bicycle kick beat Haiti Tuesday, November 17, and carried the Americans into the Concacaf Nations League semifinals against Mexico, and ESPN describes players and fans celebrating a departure no United States coach has had before. Steve Cherundolo runs the December camp on an interim basis while U.S. Soccer searches for a permanent replacement, and the change reopens the midfield to fringe players who fell out of Pochettino's plans.

team_usa.title: The NWSL Championship Lands at Audi Field
team_usa.latest_developments: ESPN published its championship predictions Friday, November 20, naming Washington Spirit forward Trinity Rodman the player to watch for Saturday's final.
team_usa.summary: The Washington Spirit host the Kansas City Current in the National Women's Soccer League Championship Saturday, November 21, at Audi Field in Washington, the Spirit's third straight trip to the final. Rodman, the United States forward, called winning at home a full-circle moment that "would mean everything," and the league reaches its title game with record revenue and unresolved stadium and scheduling problems.

team_usa.latest_developments: United States forward Daryl Dike suffered an injury minutes after he came on as a substitute Thursday, November 19, as FC Cincinnati rallied past Orlando City 3-1 in the MLS Cup Eastern Conference wild-card match.
team_usa.summary: Dike, the American striker whose career has run through repeated injury layoffs, lasted only minutes in Orlando City's elimination game. The setback clouds his availability as United States coaching and roster plans reset after Mauricio Pochettino's departure for Manchester United.
